epics.title: Error-handling architecture: Result<T,RtError> rollout
epics.description: Replace throw-and-catch-substring-match for routine user-error flows with a typed Result<T, RtError> ADT in src/RoslynTools/Core/. epics.title: rt suggest — LLM-friendly command discovery and cross-linking
epics.description: Make the rt command catalog queryable by natural-language task. Adds a flat top-level rt suggest <task> meta-command (BM25 + hand-curated synonyms + JSON/text output), a SeeAlso field on RtCommandInfo for inverse/workflow/sibling cross-links, and reuses the same BM25 engine to fix unknown-command parse errors with 'did you mean' suggestions. Purely additive — no command moves or renames.

epics.title: Complete thin-host-adapter migration
epics.description: Give every ordinary command one host-neutral application definition and typed application port so CLI, MCP, daemon, and future hosts invoke the same validated operation. Complete the 55-command rollout, delete CliCommandBridge, and remove the RoslynTools.Mcp → RoslynTools.Cli project reference.
epics.notes: ADR-0003 and ADR-0007 supersede the original native-MCP-handler direction. Canonical execution plan: docs/command-application-port-migration.md plus docs/command-port-migration-groups.tsv. Sequence: serial shared foundation (US-143), parallel read-only groups (US-095/096) and mutation groups (US-097), serial bridge deletion and physical decoupling (US-098). US-099 is consolidated into US-098; do not promote CLI builders or CliCommandBridge into a renamed shared project.

epics.title: Command consistency consolidation — checklist becomes compiler-enforced
epics.description: Roll up EP-007, EP-009, EP-011, and EP-012 into one consistent command surface: typed application definitions and ports, generic host adapters, centralized input/output policy, and architecture-enforced parity across all commands.
epics.notes: P1 strategic outcome epic. See docs/consistency-roadmap.md for current sequencing. ADR-0007 replaces the former native-handler rollout with a serial application-contract foundation, parallel R0-R5/M0-M4 port conversion, bridge deletion, and physical host decoupling.

epics.title: Semantic codebase exploration
epics.description: Add read-only codebase exploration commands that combine Roslyn-derived structure with optional local embeddings. Embeddings retrieve likely families and neighbors; Roslyn remains the source of truth for symbols, facts, references, and any reported convention deviation.
epics.notes: Spawned from 2026-05-25 design discussion after evaluating Tome-style local embeddings. Scope is advisory/exploratory only: no automated edits, no embedding-only findings. Composes with EP-011 suggest and EP-012 host-neutral application ports so agents can ask natural-language questions about unfamiliar C# solutions and receive structured, verifiable results.

userStories.title: Superseded: introduce a shared read-only command handler wrapper
userStories.description: [DISPOSITION: SUPERSEDED-BY US-143] The useful intent—one execution boundary for solution loading, cancellation, error mapping, and rendering—is now part of the host-neutral application-port foundation. acceptanceCriteria: A new class src/RoslynTools/Cli/Handlers/ReadOnlyCommandHandler.cs (or similar) provides a single async entry point: HandleAsync<TInput, TOutput>(RtContext context, TInput input, Func<Solution, TInput, CancellationToken, Task<Result<TOutput, RtError>>> body) where: solution is loaded once from RtContext.Solution, the body callback receives the loaded solution + input + cancellation token, the Result is mapped to (stdout=JSON of TOutput on Ok, stderr=Error: {message} + exit 1 on Err).

The wrapper owns: solution load (via the existing IWorkspaceSessionFactory from US-053), cancellation token propagation from Console.CancelKeyPress, timing/diagnostic logging via RtLog.Debug, exception-to-exit-code mapping for the typed catch ladder from US-077.

No match: return RtError.NotFound with the query input in Context["query"].
Kind mismatch: input matches a symbol whose kind doesn't satisfy ExpectedKind — return RtError.NotFound with Context["foundKind"] set so the caller can produce a precise error message.

AmbiguityPolicy.PromptViaDecisions integrates with the existing DecisionStore: when set, an ambiguous match writes pending entries to the decisions YAML and returns RtError.AmbiguousMatch (caller maps to exit code 2).

As an rt user, I want common CLI options (--solution, --symbol, --file, --dry-run, --json, --decisions, --threshold, --top, --sort) to be constructed by shared factories so option names, descriptions, defaults, and aliases stay consistent across commands. Each factory method returns a fully-configured System.CommandLine.Option<T> with: consistent name, consistent description text, consistent default, and any required Alias[] (e.g. --solution accepts -s alias everywhere or nowhere — pick one and apply).

Vocabulary contract: option names are standardised across commands — e.g. --symbol means 'symbol name or FQN to operate on' everywhere it appears; --file means 'a single source file path' everywhere it appears; --top means 'limit output to N entries after sorting' everywhere it appears. Help text for migrated commands is unchanged in behaviour but the wording is now consistent across the catalog (e.g. --solution help reads the same in every command's --help).

Aliases: where two commands had different aliases for the same conceptual flag (e.g. --sln vs --solution-path), the factory picks one canonical and reuses; the discarded alias either becomes a deprecation alias or is removed if no usage exists.

Bm25Scorer scores each command against the tokenised query across three fields: Name (and its synonyms) at weight 3.0×, WhenToUse at weight 1.0×, Examples (joined) at weight 0.3×.
Tokenisation: split on whitespace + punctuation, lowercase, drop a small fixed stopword set {a, an, the, is, of, to, in, for, this, that, all}.
BM25 length normalisation prevents a long WhenToUse with one match from dominating a short WhenToUse with one match; k1 and b parameters use standard defaults (k1=1.2, b=0.75).
Output flags: --top N (default 3), --json (explicit override).
Text mode (default at TTY): numbered list, each entry shows name + score + first line of WhenToUse + one example. Colour the name (reuse DumpHelpCommand colour helpers).
JSON mode (--json or stdout not a TTY): array of { name, score, category, whenToUse, example, allExamples }. Designed for LLM ingestion.
Default behaviour: when stdout is not a TTY, emit JSON (matches CLAUDE.md 'read-only inspection commands: JSON to stdout' convention). --json flag forces JSON regardless.
Exit code: 0 always — empty results are a valid answer (a JSON empty array). No exit-1 / exit-2 paths in this command.

Synonym map seed: ~10 high-traffic mismatches — safe-delete←{delete,remove}, replace-datetime←{datetime,utcnow,timeprovider}, convert-static-class←{destatic,to instance,instance class}, convert-to-record←{record,to record}, make-async←{async,task}, extract-method←{extract block,pull out method}, find-callers←{callers,who calls}, find-refs←{references,uses of,usages}, outline←{list members,type members}, describe←{type shape,interface members}. userStories.title: Unknown-command fallback: reuse Bm25Scorer to suggest matches on parse errors
userStories.description: As an LLM agent typing a hallucinated or semantically-correct-but-wrong command name (rt destatic-class, rt rm-method, rt rename-symbol), I want rt to suggest the closest real command via the same BM25 engine that powers rt suggest, so I can recover without reading the full help page. System.CommandLine middleware that runs after parse-error detection.
acceptanceCriteria: System.CommandLine middleware registered in App.RunCoreAsync near the existing exception handler runs AFTER parsing and detects 'unknown command' parse errors at the root or group level.

When an unknown token is detected at a top-level or group context, the middleware: (a) emits a single 'Error: <token> is not a recognised command.' line to stderr; (b) runs Bm25Scorer.Score(App.Commands.Select(c => c.Info).ToList(), unknownToken, top: 3) to get ranked candidates; (c) if any candidate scores above a configurable threshold, prints 'Did you mean one of these?' followed by each candidate's name + first-line WhenToUse; (d) prints 'Or run: rt suggest "<task in plain English>"' as a recovery hint; (e) sets context.ExitCode = 1.

When no candidate scores above the threshold (gibberish input), the 'Did you mean' block is suppressed — only the 'is not a recognised command' line + 'Or run: rt suggest ...' hint appears. Printing low-confidence suggestions for gibberish is worse than printing nothing.
Threshold lives in Bm25Scorer as a tunable constant (e.g. MinSuggestionScore); tests pin the threshold by exercising the gibberish case.
The pure-function Bm25Scorer is shared with the rt suggest command (Story 1) — the middleware is just another caller of the same engine; the seeded synonyms apply automatically.
Output channel: stderr per CLAUDE.md 'diagnostics to stderr' convention. Exit code 1 consistent with other user-error exits.
JSON mode honour: if --json was parsed cleanly before the parse error, the 'Did you mean' block is JSON; otherwise plain text.

Theory test tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/UnknownCommandFallbackTests.cs pins (typed-token, expected-top-result) pairs: ('destatic-class','convert-static-class'), ('rm-method','inline-method' or 'safe-delete' depending on tuning), ('rename-symbol','rename'), ('seal','make-sealed'), ('blah',null /*gibberish — no high-scoring suggestion*/).
Existing System.CommandLine UseTypoCorrections() still works for short-Levenshtein typos; this middleware is the layer above for semantic matches that Levenshtein won't catch.
Backwards-compat: invocations that already succeed (every existing command) are unchanged; no measurable startup overhead from the middleware on the happy path (BM25 only runs on parse failure).
dotnet build clean; dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean; existing tests pass; new theory tests green.

Dogfood smoke: rt destatic-class prints 'Did you mean convert-static-class?' to stderr and exits 1; rt blah-blah-blah prints only the 'not a recognised command' line + 'rt suggest' hint and exits 1; rt rename --help still works (no false positives on known commands).
userStories.notes: Fourth of 4 stories under EP-011. Source plan step 11. Highest-leverage piece of the epic — most invalid invocations happen because the LLM guessed a name, and the right answer is usually one BM25 score away. Depends on Story 1 (BM25 engine + synonyms) landing first.

userStories.title: Stable fix IDs in dry-run + --apply / --skip filters for batch mutation commands
userStories.description: As an LLM agent or interactive user reviewing a batch rt refactor --dry-run, I want each proposed fix labelled with a stable deterministic ID, and I want to re-invoke the command with --apply <ids,...> or --skip <ids,...> to land exactly the subset I've decided is safe. Without this, accepting 5 of 8 proposed make-sealed changes requires hand-editing or splitting the batch by symbol name.
acceptanceCriteria: Every fix proposed by a batch mutation command (make-sealed, add-null-checks, add-global-import, convert-console-logging, replace-xunit-asserts, replace-datetime, add-xml-doc) is tagged with an 8-char hex fix ID derived from SHA-256 over (commandName + targetSymbolFqnOrRepoRelativePath + mutationKind); the ID is deterministic across runs as long as the inputs haven't changed.
When the target has no FQN (file-scoped operations), the hash falls back to repo-relative path + mutation kind — stable across runs as long as the file isn't moved/renamed.
Dry-run text output prefixes each diff section with `[fix <id>]` on its own line above the `--- path` header so the ID is grep-pable.
Dry-run JSON output (for commands that already emit JSON, or as a follow-up for those that don't) wraps each fix in `{ id, command, target, files: [{ path, diff }] }`.
A `--apply <id,id,...>` option, when present, narrows the applied set to fixes whose ID is in the list; unknown IDs are reported to stderr and exit 1.
A `--skip <id,id,...>` option, when present, applies all fixes except those listed; unknown IDs are reported to stderr and exit 1.
Passing both --apply and --skip in the same invocation is a usage error: exit 1 with a clear stderr message.
Neither --apply nor --skip require --dry-run to have been run first; IDs are deterministic so the user can compute them once and pass them later.
When --apply selects zero fixes (empty list or all IDs unknown), the command exits 0 with `No changes.` (existing no-op message) rather than failing.

Single-target commands (rename, move, extract-method, inline-method, safe-delete) emit a single fix ID in their dry-run header for consistency, but --apply/--skip are *not* registered on them (no benefit and adds parse-time noise).

Integration tests under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Mutation/ cover: (a) determinism — same input twice produces same ID; (b) --apply picks subset; (c) --skip drops subset; (d) both flags error; (e) unknown ID errors; (f) ID stability across an unrelated edit elsewhere in the project.
dotnet build clean; dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean; existing tests pass.
userStories.notes: P2. Centralise ID generation in a new FixId helper in src/RoslynTools/Core/. Each batch command's service exposes the candidate fix list (already does internally — just needs to lift it before SolutionWriter.ApplyChangesAsync) so the command host can apply --apply/--skip filtering before workspace changes are computed. Option registration: extend CommandOptionFactory with CreateApplyOption()/CreateSkipOption() and a shared parser. Scope: batch commands only (single-target commands gain nothing from --apply/--skip). Out of scope for MVP: backporting --apply/--skip to single-target commands; JSON envelope for commands that today emit only text diffs (track as a follow-up under EP-007 if useful). userStories.title: rt analyze conventions: embedding-assisted C# pattern and deviation discovery
userStories.description:
[DISPOSITION: DEFERRED] rt analyze conventions / EP-014 exploratory — defer; research-flagged.

As an agent exploring an unfamiliar C# solution, I want `rt analyze conventions` to discover repeated implementation families and highlight likely deviations from local convention, so I can find one-off drift without manually reading every command, handler, service, or result model.
acceptanceCriteria: New read-only command `rt analyze conventions --solution <sln>` exists, implements IAnalyzeCommand, and follows the host-neutral application-port pattern: ConventionAnalysisService in src/RoslynTools/Services/, shared request/result/definition, thin CLI binder, and generic MCP projection returning structured JSON.

The service builds a Roslyn-derived code fact index for C# type and method declarations: symbol FQN, DocumentationCommentId, kind, namespace, containing type, base type, implemented interfaces, attributes, accessibility, modifiers, constructor dependency types, member signatures, XML doc summary/remarks/param/returns text when present, file path, line span, and a deterministic content hash.

Public method entries use the checked-in XML documentation as canonical semantic text; the index embeds XML docs plus signature/metadata, and never overwrites human-authored public docs with generated summaries.

Generated summaries are permitted only for undocumented non-public methods or aggregate type/family summaries, and every generated summary is marked as generated/disposable in the stored index record.

The service creates one embedding document per indexed type and one embedding document per indexed method from Roslyn-derived facts, not arbitrary raw source chunks. Type embedded text includes signatures, member summaries, interfaces/base types, attributes, constructor dependencies, and a compact vocabulary of method/member names. Method embedded text includes XML docs, signature, containing type, parameter/return metadata, attributes, and selected deterministic call/dependency facts.

The symbol index and vector index are separate stores keyed by symbol id plus content/doc hash; vector hits may retrieve candidates, but all reported facts and every future mutation must re-resolve the current Roslyn symbol before acting.
Index freshness is enforced: changed method bodies, signatures, or XML docs invalidate the corresponding indexed record until rebuilt; stale vector records are ignored rather than trusted.

The existing public Core XML-doc architecture rule is strengthened with a checked-in review index file (docs/public-core-method-review-index.tsv) that hashes public Core method implementations and requires reviewed=true. When a public Core method implementation changes, the failing architecture test prints the exact replacement line plus instructions to review behaviour, side effects, dry-run semantics, errors, and return value against the XML docs before updating the index.

Embedding support is optional and provider-backed behind an interface (for example IEmbeddingProvider). If no provider is configured, the command exits 1 with a clear stderr message unless `--fallback structural` is passed; no network dependency is required by default.
`--scope <namespace-or-path-prefix>` restricts analysis to a namespace or file path prefix; omitting it analyzes the whole solution.
`--query <natural-language-family>` filters candidate clusters by semantic intent, e.g. `--query "MCP handlers"`, `--query "CLI command classes"`, or `--query "services that mutate solutions"`.
`--baseline <type-or-fqn>` analyzes nearest neighbors to a known type and reports deviations relative to that local family, e.g. `--baseline RoslynTools.Mcp.Handlers.FindReferencesHandler`.

Default mode clusters similar type documents using embeddings, then compares each candidate against its nearest neighbors using deterministic Roslyn facts. Embeddings may select neighbors, but every reported deviation must cite a concrete Roslyn-derived fact difference.

Output JSON shape includes: analyzedTypes, clusters[], outliers[], diagnostics[]. Each cluster includes label, representativeTypes[], memberCount, and confidence. Each outlier includes symbol, file, line, nearestNeighbors[], reason, confidence, and evidence[].

Deviation reasons are evidence-first and non-authoritative: examples include missing interface/base type, inconsistent command capability marker, different constructor dependency shape, missing static Info metadata, different handler ToolName naming pattern, missing JsonSchemaBuilder usage, or result model not implementing the expected output interface.

The command labels findings as `suggestion`, not `violation`, unless the deviation is already backed by an existing deterministic architecture rule. No refactor is applied or suggested as safe solely because of embedding similarity.
`--min-confidence` filters low-confidence outliers; default threshold is conservative enough that singleton clusters and weak neighbor sets are suppressed.
`--top N` limits outlier output deterministically after ranking by confidence, then symbol FQN; omitting --top returns all findings above threshold.
MCP tool name mirrors CLI command naming convention as `conventions` (hyphen to underscore if needed) and exposes input schema for solution, scope, query, baseline, top, minConfidence, and fallback.
Unit tests cover fact extraction on synthetic C# projects: command classes, MCP handlers, services, and result models produce expected CodeTypeFacts without loading external files.
Unit tests cover deterministic deviation comparison independent of embeddings by passing fake neighbor sets into the service.
Integration test against RoslynTools.slnx with a fake deterministic embedding provider returns clusters for Commands and MCP handlers and produces stable JSON with no stdout/stderr mixing.

When the embedding provider is unavailable, test verifies clean handled failure and verifies `--fallback structural` still runs a deterministic grouping pass by namespace/interfaces/base-type/member-shape.
Documentation added to docs/ or CLAUDE.md explaining the hybrid rule: embeddings retrieve candidate families; Roslyn verifies and explains; mutations remain out of scope.

userStories.title: Daemon Stage 3 — workspace cache with git-HEAD invalidation + operational hardening
userStories.description:
As an agent dogfooding rt, I want the daemon to cache the loaded MSBuild solution between commands (keyed by solution path + git HEAD) and invalidate it on change, so a tight rt loop avoids the ~3-5s solution reload per call. Today the daemon caches nothing (DaemonServer.cs has no cache) — every routed command reloads the solution, so the daemon only saves process-startup cost, not the slow MSBuild solution-load cost. This story also folds in the operational rough edges found while shipping US-117 (2026-05-27), since they make the daemon painful to run and were blocking dogfooding.

DESIGN RE-CHECK (as-built, 2026-05-27): The cache key is already available — every DaemonRequest carries GitState(Head, Dirty, IndexMtime) from GitService.GetState (reads .git/HEAD + .git/index mtime directly). The integration seam is IWorkspaceSessionFactory (src/RoslynTools/Core/IWorkspaceSessionFactory.cs), registered as a singleton in Bootstrap.cs:23-24, today implemented by WorkspaceLoader which reloads on every GetSolutionAsync/LoadWorkspaceAsync call. CENTRAL HAZARD: commands that call LoadWorkspaceAsync wrap it in using (workspace) (e.g. RenameCommand.cs:73-75) which DISPOSES the workspace after each command. A cached workspace must NOT be disposed per-command — either the caching factory hands out a non-owning Workspace handle, or those commands move to the solution-only GetSolutionAsync API (the interface contract already says callers must not dispose). Resolve this before writing the cache.
acceptanceCriteria: CACHE: the daemon holds at most one loaded solution per (solutionPath, gitHead) key; a second request with the same key reuses it without reloading.
CACHE: a request whose git HEAD differs from the cached key triggers eviction (dispose old workspace) + reload.
CACHE: eviction also fires when any .csproj/.props/.slnx under the solution dir has an mtime newer than the cached load time (covers uncommitted edits where HEAD is unchanged).

CACHE: per-command using (workspace) disposal must not dispose a cached workspace — migrate LoadWorkspaceAsync callers (RenameCommand.cs:73-75 etc.) to the non-owning GetSolutionAsync seam, or make the caching factory return a non-owning handle. Document the choice.

CACHE: cache logic lives behind IWorkspaceSessionFactory (a daemon-scoped caching implementation), so in-process runs are unchanged and the NoDirectConsoleUse + DI singleton ownership rules still hold.
OBS: rt daemon status reports cached solutions with key (path + short HEAD), age, and last-used.
PERF (integration test): two back-to-back inspect calls against the same solution through the daemon — the second is at least 5x faster than the first.

ROUGH EDGE — stop --force: rt daemon stop --force skips the graceful pipe round-trip (which today blocks up to ~15s on a wedged daemon, DaemonCommand.cs:77-134) and instead kills the PID from the state file and removes ~/.rt/daemon.json immediately.

ROUGH EDGE — build interference: the GenerateCommandsMd post-build target (RoslynTools.Cli.csproj:81-88) runs rt dump-help against the Release/Debug rt.dll; a running daemon holding that assembly locked on Windows must not block or corrupt the build. Fix so a build never hangs/fails because a daemon is alive (e.g. dump-help fast-path that never routes to the daemon + does not lock the output, or build stops/ignores the daemon).

ROUGH EDGE — start readiness: rt daemon start gives a clear, bounded failure if the spawned --daemon-serve process never writes daemon.json within the poll window (DaemonCommand.cs:28-75, 10s poll) — surface the daemon.log tail on timeout instead of a silent give-up, and ensure a failed-init spawn cannot leave a half-state.

userStories.title: rt inspect find-unused: framework-instantiated types reported as unused (xUnit fixtures, DI/convention-registered services)
userStories.description: As a user running find-unused before a safe-delete pass, I want types that a framework constructs reflectively to be excluded, so that the output is signal rather than noise and never invites deleting live code. find-unused equates 'zero SymbolFinder references' with 'dead'. A type constructed by a container or test runner rather than by explicit `new` has no source references, so it is reported as unused even though deleting it breaks the build or silently drops behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: A class is not reported when it or any base type declares [Fact]/[Theory] methods (inherited-only fixtures must also be excluded, e.g. a contract base class holding the [Fact]s)
A class deriving from ControllerBase or carrying [ApiController] is not reported

A type used as a type-argument in a DI registration (AddSingleton<IFoo,Foo>, AddScoped, AddTransient, AddHostedService, AddHttpClient<TI,TImpl>) is not reported — add a regression test even if FindReferencesAsync already resolves the type-argument

Scrutor assembly-scanning is handled in tiers rather than declared undetectable: interpret the readable selector chain (FromAssemblyOf<T>/FromAssemblies, AddClasses(c => c.AssignableTo<T>()), InNamespaces, WithAttribute<T>) and treat matching types as referenced; where the selector is an arbitrary lambda, suppress unused-type findings for instantiable types in the scanned assembly only (sound, localised, trades false negatives for zero false positives). See US-139 for the probe that backfills annotations.
find-unused --scope types on RoslynTools.slnx and on a solution with xUnit tests reports zero test fixtures
Findings carry confidence + reason, and the safe-delete suggestedFix is emitted only at high confidence, so an uncertain finding can never invite deleting live code
userStories.notes: P1 correctness. Root cause: FindUnusedService.ShouldExclude (src/RoslynTools/Services/FindUnusedService.cs:75-96) excludes METHODS carrying [Fact]/[Theory] (`symbol is IMethodSymbol m`) but never the CONTAINING TYPE, and has no DI/reflection awareness at all. Evidence: `find_unused --scope types` via MCP against DnDan-2nd-Edition (csharp/DnDan.slnx) returned ~30 types of which all but one (RecordedEventExtensions, a genuine finding) were xUnit test classes. SqliteEventStoreTests was among them despite having no [Fact] of its own — its [Fact]s are inherited from the EventStoreContractTests base — so keying the fix on directly-declared attributes only would still miss it. Severity is raised by each finding emitting a `rt refactor safe-delete` suggestedFix, so the false positives actively invite deleting live code. The xUnit half is directly verified; the DI half follows from the same root cause and bites specifically on convention/assembly-scan registration, since explicit AddSingleton<IFoo,Foo>() does create a resolvable reference. | Design note: find-unused's error costs are asymmetric — it triggers deletion, so a false positive (live code called dead) is far worse than a false negative (dead code missed). Bias conservative wherever the analysis is blind.

userStories.title: rt analyze probe-di: opt-in DI probe that lists registered types invisible to static analysis
userStories.description: As a maintainer of a solution using assembly-scanning DI, I want an opt-in probe that reports which registered implementation types carry no static reference and no reflective-use annotation, so that I can backfill annotations once and let the purely-static find-unused stay correct afterwards. The probe is a generator, not part of the analysis path: find-unused itself never executes user code.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze probe-di --entrypoint <Type.Method> --solution <sln> invokes ONLY the named registration method against a fresh ServiceCollection and enumerates ServiceDescriptors — it does not boot the host or run the application

Reports each ServiceDescriptor.ImplementationType that has zero SymbolFinder references AND carries none of [UsedImplicitly], [DynamicDependency] (targeting it via typeof), or an ILLink descriptor entry
Types registered via a factory delegate (ImplementationType == null) are reported as unprobeable rather than silently skipped

Each finding carries a suggestedFix whose commandLine invokes `rt refactor add-dynamic-dependency` (US-140) for that type — probe-di is in the analyze group and stays read-only; it never mutates source
The probe requires a built solution; it fails with a clear message rather than a load exception when assemblies are missing
probe-di is never invoked implicitly by find-unused
userStories.notes: P2. Child of US-138; addresses the assembly-scanning hole that static analysis alone cannot close. Key design: the probe's output is durable static facts (annotations), so it runs occasionally rather than on every analysis — this is what makes executing a slice of user code acceptable. Narrow blast radius: invoke the registration extension method only, not the app lifecycle. Annotation choice matters — [DynamicDependency] goes on the CONSUMER pointing at the target via typeof, which SymbolFinder already counts, so it is self-fixing; [UsedImplicitly] sits on the type but needs a JetBrains.Annotations package reference plus explicit Tier-3 support in ShouldExclude; [DynamicallyAccessedMembers] is the wrong shape (it annotates Type-valued parameters/fields, not declarations). Known hole: factory registrations expose no ImplementationType, but their lambda bodies usually contain `new X()`, which is already a static reference — so the probe's real yield is Scrutor scans and AddHostedService<T>. | Read/write split: probe-di reports and links; US-140 applies. Keeps the analyze group read-only per repo convention and lets a user review findings before any source changes.

userStories.title: rt refactor add-dynamic-dependency: annotate a composition root so reflectively-registered types stay visible
userStories.description: As a maintainer acting on probe-di findings, I want a refactor that adds [DynamicDependency] for a reflectively-registered type onto its composition root, so that the type gains a real source reference and every static tool — find-unused, trimming, NativeAOT — stops treating it as dead. Applying the annotation is the durable fix; the probe only finds what needs it.
acceptanceCriteria: rt refactor add-dynamic-dependency --type <fqn> --root <Type.Method> --solution <sln> adds [DynamicDependency(DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.PublicConstructors, typeof(<type>))] to the named composition-root method
--dry-run prints the diff and applies nothing (repo convention for destructive refactors)
Adds the System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis using directive when absent, and adds no package reference (the attribute is in the BCL)
Re-running is idempotent: an existing [DynamicDependency] for the same type is not duplicated
After applying, rt inspect find-unused no longer reports the annotated type — because typeof(<type>) is a real reference SymbolFinder already resolves, with no special-casing in ShouldExclude
Accepts repeated --type arguments so a full probe-di run can be actioned in one invocation
userStories.notes: P2. Completes the US-138 → US-139 → US-140 chain: detect the blindness, probe for what static analysis cannot see, then make it statically visible for good. The annotation is chosen so the fix is self-reinforcing rather than tool-specific — [DynamicDependency] is BCL, needs no package, and helps trimming/NativeAOT for the same reason it helps find-unused: it turns an invisible reflective edge into a real typeof reference. Verify the acceptance test asserts find-unused's behaviour AFTER the refactor, so the chain is proven end to end rather than assumed.
